chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, that Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
used to enter the bathhouse, so he would wax his armpit alone when he was in need of that alone.
ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on waxing the armpit alone in the bathhouse according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: This narration from Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes the permissibility of private grooming in the bathhouse, reflecting the Shia emphasis on *satr* (modesty/covering) even during acts of purification. It underscores the principle that while communal hygiene is encouraged, individual modesty takes precedence when one is alone, aligning with the broader jurisprudential focus on maintaining dignity in daily rituals.

en.hubeali: Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub that,
‘Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> used to enter the bathhouse, so he<sup>asws</sup> would wax his<sup>asws</sup> armpit alone when he<sup>asws</sup> was needy to that alone’.
en.sarwar: 6. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from ibn Mahbub from Yunus ibn Ya‘qub who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam,
whenever needed would go to the bathhouse only to apply lime paste to his underarms.’”
